# Retrospective attainability after inspecting policy results

Diagnose the source of the observed precision and recall deficits. This additional analysis uses the evaluation labels deliberately and never proposes a deployable policy. Reconstruct the exact same held-out course pools, risk scores and feasible female seat counts as the screen. For each count tabulate actual dropout cases among the two selected score prefixes. Independently compute an optimistic assignment's counts after putting all observed positives first within each group at the same seat count. Keep identical seats and prefix requirements. For each representation and each number of female cases captured across courses, compute the greatest male capture count by dynamic programming. Require the exact integer precision floor corresponding to at most a one-point loss versus realized unrestricted precision. Return maximal worst-group recall, number of feasible states, a witness with course seat counts, and shortfall of the frozen policy. Distinguish feasibility at the retrospective precision floor from the different score-utility constraint used by the live policies. Interpret as a conditional upper bound and report results even if no feasible state exists.
